concerns: The manuscript contains severe contextual incongruities that undermine scientific validity: the novelty section claims improvements in packet delivery ratio, end-to-end delay, energy consumption, throughput, and network lifetime, which are wireless sensor network metrics irrelevant to biometric recognition.

The statistical test section describes ANOVA for student performance prediction and references an unrelated model acronym (LKMILBDC), indicating copy-paste text from an unrelated domain and casting doubt on the reported statistical validation.

The evaluation uses PSNR, an image reconstruction quality metric, as a primary performance measure for a biometric classification model without scientific justification, and the results text mislabels PSNR values as sensitivity, indicating unreliable reporting.

The manuscript does not establish evaluator independence: the same AAM-Softmax loss optimized during training is used to shape the embedding space, and the reported classification metrics are derived from the same model's decision outputs without independent human or external benchmark validation.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The manuscript displays major scientific flaws, including incongruous text from wireless sensor networking (packet delivery ratio, network lifetime) and educational data mining (student performance prediction ANOVA), as well as evaluating recognition models on image reconstruction metrics (PSNR) without clear scientific justification. These severe inconsistencies preclude confidence in the technical execution and validity of the results.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The manuscript contains severe contextual incongruities that undermine scientific validity: the novelty section claims improvements in packet delivery ratio, end-to-end delay, energy consumption, throughput, and network lifetime, which are wireless sensor network metrics irrelevant to biometric recognition.

The statistical test section describes ANOVA for student performance prediction and references an unrelated model acronym (LKMILBDC), indicating copy-paste text from an unrelated domain and casting doubt on the reported statistical validation.

The evaluation uses PSNR, an image reconstruction quality metric, as a primary performance measure for a biometric classification model without scientific justification, and the results text mislabels PSNR values as sensitivity, indicating unreliable reporting.

The manuscript does not establish evaluator independence: the same AAM-Softmax loss optimized during training is used to shape the embedding space, and the reported classification metrics are derived from the same model's decision outputs without independent human or external benchmark validation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported statistical test section references student performance prediction and an unrelated model acronym, while the results text mislabels PSNR values as sensitivity, so the reported measurements do not reliably corroborate the headline biometric recognition gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Classification metrics (accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity) and PSNR computed on cross-validation splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Additive Angular Margin Loss (AAM-Softmax) optimized with Adam backpropagation on face and voice spectrogram features.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The reported results show substantial improvements, but the alignment with the biometric authentication claims is severely undermined by nonsensical metric claims (e.g., packet delivery ratio, end-to-end delay) and copy-paste text from unrelated domains.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The experimental evaluation reports PSNR for face images and voice signals without explaining why a reconstruction/image quality metric applies to a classification model, alongside precision, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy across varying sample sizes. The tables and text exhibit anomalous descriptions, and the ANOVA description specifically references student performance prediction instead of biometric authentication.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard classification evaluation metrics (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity) were computed on held-out test splits from 10-fold cross-validation.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Classification accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity, and PSNR across cross-validation splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Additive Angular Margin Loss (AAM-Softmax) optimized with Adam backpropagation on face and voice spectrogram features.

primary.limitations: The authors note testing on only a single dataset and omitting time and memory benchmarks, but do not address the pervasive conceptual contradictions and incongruent metrics in the text.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology presents architectural descriptions combining CNN feature extractors, ViT self-attention, cross-modal attention, and additive angular margin softmax loss. However, the manuscript contains severe contextual incongruities, such as claiming network lifetime and packet delivery ratio improvements for biometric recognition, and referring to student performance prediction and an unrelated model acronym (LKMILBDC) in the statistical test section.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript displays major scientific flaws, including incongruous text from wireless sensor networking (packet delivery ratio, network lifetime) and educational data mining (student performance prediction ANOVA), as well as evaluating recognition models on image reconstruction metrics (PSNR) without clear scientific justification. These severe inconsistencies preclude confidence in the technical execution and validity of the results.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper proposes CNN-AAViT, a hybrid convolutional neural network and vision transformer architecture using additive angular margin loss for audio-visual multimodal biometric recognition evaluated on the MSU-AVIS dataset.
